name: pimi-visualize

<!-- formats:start (generated by packages/protocol/scripts/generate-visualize-formats.mjs; do not edit) -->

Pimi chat renders these fenced code blocks inline in a reply. Use whichever shows the answer best.

pimi-vega: one Vega-Lite v6 spec as JSON.
- Rows go inline in data.values. Nothing can load: a "url" or "href" property anywhere in the spec fails the block, and so does a raw Vega spec.
- Pimi fits the width, applies its light or dark theme, shows tooltips, and shows the spec's title above the chart.

pimi-view: JSON {"title", "root", optional "id"} where root is a node. Each node is an object with a "type" and these fields:
- stack: children; optional direction "column" (default) or "row"
- grid: children; optional positive columns (default 2), fewer when narrow
- section: title, children
- metric: label, value (string); optional delta (string), tone, hint, trend (numbers drawn as a sparkline)
- table: columns [{label, optional align "start" or "end"}] with distinct labels, rows of strings or numbers, one cell per column
- progress: label, value, max; optional tone
- text: content; optional tone, emphasis "normal", "strong" or "subtle"
- badge: label; optional tone
- flow: nodes [{id, label, optional detail, lane, kind, tone}], edges [{from, to, optional label}] naming node ids; optional direction "right" (default) or "down", lanes [{id, label}]. A kind is one of step, user, agent, service, data, file, queue, tool, code, external, secret. Cycles are allowed; an edge from a node to itself is not
- sequence: participants [{id, label}] in column order, steps in time order. A step is a message {from, to, label, optional reply (true draws a dashed return arrow), tone}, a note {note}, or a group {group, steps}: a labelled frame around a loop, an optional part, or one branch of an alternative. from and to name participant ids and may be the same participant
A tone is one of neutral, positive, negative, warning. Every text field is plain text: no Markdown, HTML, links, images, or colors. Pimi lays out flows and sequences itself.
A later block with the same id replaces the earlier one in the same reply.

pimi-html: one HTML document or fragment, run in a sandboxed frame.
- No network, storage, or navigation: remote scripts, styles, fonts, images, and fetch fail. Put the CSS, JavaScript, and data in the block.
- Pimi sets the page background, text color, and font for its light and dark themes and provides these custom properties: --pimi-bg, --pimi-surface, --pimi-fg, --pimi-muted, --pimi-border, --pimi-accent, --pimi-accent-fg, --pimi-font, --pimi-mono.
- The frame is the reply's width, about 360 px on a phone. It follows the content's height up to 640 px, then scrolls, so 100vh has no meaning.
- The <title> is shown above the frame. Three backticks inside the block end it.
- pimi-artifact holds {"title", "path"} and runs a saved .html file the same way, with the path relative to the working directory.

mermaid: a Mermaid diagram, scaled down to fit the reply's width.

<!-- formats:end -->
